newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court to resume B Band ruling next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court to resume B Band ruling next week.

text.p: Brazil's supreme court justices will resume issuing their rulings next week on whether or not the government's plan to privatize B Band cellular telephone services is unconstitutional, a court spokeswoman said.
"The ruling should begin again next week because today is the last day for receiving complementary information," Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) spokeswoman Vera Keller said.

Left-wing political parties have challenged the constitutionality of the government's plan to offer private groups 15-year concessions to run cellular services on a so-called B Band frequency in 10 regional areas.
The B Band program represents the first phase of telecommunications privatization in Brazil. Private groups have been asked to submit bids for the concessions on April 7.

The high court suspended the ruling process last month after some of its members expressed doubts on technical points of the government's B Band concession plan. The ruling was held up for 10 working days to ask for more information.
Keller said the government had already provided the STF with the data it required and further information from the Senate was due Friday.
The STF would probably resume its ruling Wednesday or Thursday, the two days of the week when it holds full sessions, the spokeswoman said.
So far, only one of the tribunal's 10 members has voted on the first of five alleged inconstitutionalities raised by the opposition. He ruled against the opposition.
Earlier this month, a lower-level court threw out a trade union's request for an injunction to halt the B Band program.
